results.title: Pentagon obligates 97.5% of OBBBA funds ahead of lame-duck spending debate
results.description: As lawmakers prepare to debate federal defense spending in the upcoming lame-duck session following midterm elections, the Pentagon has announced it has obligated 97.5% of its $152.4 billion in One Big Beautiful Bill Act funding before the end of fiscal year 2026, though the remaining $3.9 billion faces an estimated $323.7 million cut under the mandatory defense sequester. The Defense Department announced today that it obligated $148.5 billion in OBBBA funding by Sept. 30, describing the obligation rate as evidence of efforts to rapidly deploy resources for combat readiness and force modernization. The department didn't address the potential sequestration impact in its announcement and didn't provide further comment when additional information was sought. A congressional staffer said the mandatory FY-27 defense sequester took effect Oct. 1 and that the 8.3% reduction applies to the remaining $3.9 billion in unobligated OBBBA funds, resulting in an estimated $323.7 million reduction. The OBBBA provided approximately $152 billion for defense priorities including munitions, shipbuilding, aircraft, air and missile defense and other military modernization efforts. The Pentagon's component-level obligation figures show the military services obligated more than 98% of their respective allocations, while other department components had a lower execution rate. The Army obligated $10.5 billion, or 98.1%, of its $10.7 billion allocation. The Navy obligated $48.7 billion, or 99.2%, of its $49.2 billion allocation, while the Air Force obligated $34 billion, or 99.2%, of its $34.3 billion allocation. Other DOD components obligated $55.2 billion, or 94.9%, of their $58.1 billion allocation. The Pentagon also said it consulted Congress and reserved portions of funding for the Office of Strategic Capital, the Defense Innovation Unit and the Economic Defense Unit to preserve investment options into FY-27 and maximize use of those funds. The department did not disclose how much was reserved for those organizations. An obligation represents a legal commitment to spend funds, rather than a completed expenditure. The high OBBBA obligation rate could nevertheless make it harder for lawmakers to point to unspent Pentagon funding as a reason to question the department's need for additional resources during the lame-duck session, the congressional staffer said. The Trump administration is seeking a $1.5 trillion defense topline for FY-27, with $350 billion of the funds being sought through budgetary reconciliation. The department noted in its announcement that the current data “represents an early closeout estimate based on internal financial records” that may be adjusted by the end of the year.
